title: Add Airtable rows with AI from an attendance list
h1: add new airtable rows without rewriting existing records
description: Turn a workshop sign-in sheet into Airtable attendance rows. Match the fields, skip existing attendees and add up to ten new rows per request.
answer:
**stop typing the same attendance list twice.** give the bot your sign-in sheet and airtable destination. it matches the fields and adds up to ten new rows per request, leaving existing records alone.

row creation can run without asking. put a preview in the routine so you choose what goes in.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: the sign-in sheet becomes attendance rows.
what:
**new rows, without retyping the attendance sheet.** name the base and table. the bot lists bases and reads the table fields before matching your values. this action adds records; it doesn't repair old ones.

keep automatic conversion off for the first run. airtable otherwise tries to interpret text as dates or other values. a tidy-looking cell can still contain the wrong thing.
uses: **attendance without retyping.** add confirmed people from a finished workshop.
**equipment as it arrives.** log each new item's category and arrival date.
**expenses ready to file.** add new rows without replacing earlier entries.
**volunteer shifts.** use the confirmed sign-up list; leave unclear dates for you.

routine.message:
on saturdays at 10, read sign-in sheets added this week to the 'workshop sign-ins' folder in google drive. use the workshop attendance table in the learning sessions base.

- read its fields and find existing rows with the same session and email
- show only new rows here and ask me before writing
- add the rows i approve, up to ten at a time, then report what you saved

never overwrite a record, guess an email or use automatic field conversion. skip existing matches. if a sheet is unclear, ask me.
routine.needs: google drive read only; airtable read and write, including field reads and existing-row lookups
routine.output:
attendance saved after your confirmation

workshop: product sketching
- rue tan, rue@example.com, attended
- bela roy, bela@example.com, attended

skipped one existing match for the same session and email.

steps: **connect the two apps.** drive only needs reading. airtable needs read and write to add rows.
**name the destination.** ask which fields the attendance table expects before giving it a whole sheet.
**limit the actions.** allow lookups and row creation. leave record updates and table changes off.
**try one batch.** compare the saved names and session with the preview. pause the routine if they differ.
watch: **ten rows per request.** larger sheets need batches. airtable allows five requests per second per base.
**conversion can guess wrong.** it starts off; leave it off until unclear values have an agreed meaning.
**a retry can add everyone twice.** inspect existing rows before repeating a request with an unclear result.
**the preview is your review step.** row creation does not wait for sending approval.

faq.q: can it add more than ten airtable records?
faq.a: **yes, in batches of ten or fewer.** it must also stay within five requests per second per base.

faq.q: will creating records update a matching row?
faq.a: **no, it adds another row.** the routine reads existing records first and skips matches.

faq.q: what if a date or category does not fit?
faq.a: **ask which date or category the sheet means.** automatic conversion can interpret text, but it can pick the wrong meaning.

sources.label: Metal docs: sending and approval settings

steps: pick one finished sign-in sheet in drive
name the airtable base and table
ask for two proposed rows, without writing
match the fields and look for existing attendees

mistakes.fix: look for the same session and email before adding rows, including after a timeout.

mistakes.mistake: letting airtable guess a vague date
mistakes.fix: keep conversion off. ask which date the sign-in sheet means.

items: the session and email identify a new attendance row
each value fits the table field
the preview contains no more than ten rows

tip.text: a duplicate attendee looks harmless until you count the room twice.
